original_test_intent: Demonstrate that the mapped GB-NV-PVP PCIe path can perform five hundred genuine Gen2-to-Gen4 transitions at the required width without training, endpoint, or system errors.
original_method: Confirm end-to-end Gen4 capability and the exact Speed Change 24 action; for every numbered iteration prove a full-width Gen2 starting state, request Gen4, record intermediate training/equalization, settle to the required Gen4 width, and capture error/health deltas before permitting the next iteration; stop and recover on the first anomaly.
manual_activity: Owner/FAE approves the Gen4-capable path and Speed Change 24 recipe; an operator isolates the SUT and owns console recovery from endpoint, GPU, or host disruption.
required_inputs: Pinned NVIDIA LTSSM/NVQual Speed Change 24 configuration
Method proving Gen2/full-width at each cycle start
Gen4 request, equalization/LTSSM trajectory, required width, settle timeout, and transient rules
500-count, error-delta, abort, final-state, and recovery policy
safety_requirements: Dedicated approved SUT with stable power/cooling and out-of-band console
Validate target path, Gen2 start, and Gen4 support

Do not continue or retry automatically
agent_execution_scope: Verify tool, topology, start-state method, capability, and acceptance

engineer_actions: Approve Speed Change 24 and path capability

Review all 500 transactions and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

review_improvement: Preserves the exact Gen2-to-Gen4 repetition coverage and rejects lower-generation, end-state-only, or post-failure evidence shortcuts.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row needs two independent proofs inside every cycle: the link truly entered Gen2 first, and the complete channel then trained to full-width Gen4 without new errors. If either is inferred from a preceding cycle or a final snapshot, the tool may be reasserting the current speed rather than exercising the specified transition. Gen4 equalization can also hide marginal behavior behind a later stable state, so intermediate LTSSM/equalization and error deltas are essential. A fail-closed ledger preserves the first anomaly before further transitions change causality.
